reason: No official SWISS national net (take-home) monthly median income figure could be obtained from the Federal Statistical Office's published outputs. This is a PUBLICATION gap, not a data gap and not a fetch outage: the Swiss Earnings Structure Survey (Lohnstrukturerhebung, LSE) demonstrably DOES collect net wage data - a cantonal statistical office quotes national net wage distribution thresholds derived from it (see 020_net_monthly_income.json) - but every BFS-published LSE table reached in this research is a GROSS table, and no net median is exposed. Switzerland's structural context makes this gap harder to fill elsewhere too: federal, cantonal and municipal income taxes all apply, so there is no single national net figure to find even in principle, and any net number must be canton-specific. No net figure was invented to fill the gap.
what_specifically_blocked: BFS 'Lohnstruktur' overview page: read in full. States 'Im Jahr 2024 betrug der Medianlohn 7024 Franken brutto pro Monat' - explicitly BRUTTO. Links only to gross tables.

BFS STAT-TAB / PX-Web wage data cube index (queried directly via the PX-Web JSON API at https://www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/de/px-x-0304010000_205): returns a single table, 'Monatlicher Bruttolohn nach Grossregion, Berufsgruppe, Lebensalter und Geschlecht'. Gross. This is the decisive technical finding - the machine-readable cube index contains no net-wage table.

BFS 'Nach personenbezogenen Merkmalen' page: read. Titled 'Monatlicher Bruttolohn nach Merkmalen wie Alter, Bildungsstand, Staatsangehorigkeit und Arbeitsbewilligung'. Gross only. (Also note: a plain web fetch of this page returned an empty body and the content had to be obtained via a browser session.)
BFS 'Nach Berufsgruppen' and 'Nach Grossregionen' pages: read via search-surfaced content. All tables titled 'Monatlicher Bruttolohn ...'. Gross only.

BFS 'Lohnunterschied nach Geschlecht' page: read in full via a browser session. Searched programmatically for the string 'Nettolohn' across the page text - ZERO occurrences. The BFS gender-pay-gap analysis, which is where net wage tables appeared in the LSE 2018 edition (tables titled 'Durchschnittl. Nettolohn nach Beschaeftigungsgrad und Wirtschaftsbranche'), no longer exposes net wage figures on the accessible page for the LSE 2024 edition.

BFS Salarium (official statistical wage calculator, salarium.bfs.admin.ch): read the description. 'Salarium bietet Ihnen die Moeglichkeit, fuer ein bestimmtes Profil den monatlichen Bruttolohn und die Streuung der Loehne zu berechnen.' GROSS ONLY by design, despite the name 'Lohnrechner' which can be misread as a net calculator.
BFS 'Erwerbseinkommen' page: table titled 'Bruttoerwerbseinkommen pro Jahr ... Zentralwert (Median) ... in Franken, 2025'. Gross.

BFS 'Einkommensverteilung' page: this is the closest thing to a net measure and it was checked. It reports 'verfuegbares Aequivalenzeinkommen' (available/disposable equivalised income) from the Swiss Household Survey - 2024 median equivalised income CHF 52 893 per year, 10th percentile CHF 27 409, 90th percentile CHF 98 542. This is a net concept but it is an equivalised household income measure from a different survey (not the LSE), it is equivalised for household size, and it is household rather than individual. It is therefore not a take-home salary and was NOT recorded as one.

Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) 'Umrechnung von Nettoloehnen in Bruttoloehne AHV/IV/EO/ALV' (document 318.115, current version valid from 01.01.2026): this IS an official net-to-gross conversion table and would have qualified as category-2 evidence, but it covers ONLY the AHV/IV/EO/ALV social insurance contributions. It excludes federal, cantonal and municipal income tax, excludes BVG occupational pension, and excludes NBU and KTG. The PDF itself was not retrievable in this pass. Because it covers only part of the gross-to-net bridge it cannot produce a take-home figure, so it is recorded here as an identified but insufficient route rather than as evidence.

SECO guidance on pay registration and payroll (read): confirms the Swiss payroll structure - 'Der Arbeitgebende hat bei jeder Lohnzahlung den Anteil der Arbeitnehmenden der Sozialversicherungsbeitraege in Abzug zu bringen' - and confirms that contributions are due from the first franc of pay. No net-gross table for income tax on this page. Note also that SECO refers to a 'nationaler Lohnrechner' distinct from the FSO's Salarium; that national salary calculator was NOT located or read in this pass and is the most promising next avenue for a cantonal net figure.

FETCH FAILURES RECORDED: (a) https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/de/home/statistiken/arbeit-erwerb/loehne-erwerbseinkommen-arbeitskosten/erwerbseinkommen.html and https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/de/home/statistiken/arbeit-erwerb/loehne-erwerbseinkommen-arbeitskosten/lohnstruktur/personenbezogene-merkmale.html both returned an empty body to the plain web-fetch tool and required a browser session instead; (b) https://sozialversicherungen.admin.ch/de/f/6465 loaded but the target document was not present at that navigation level - the page returned 'Auf dieser Navigationsebene befinden sich keine Dokumente'; (c) the BSV conversion-table PDF at document 318.115 was not successfully retrieved.
recommended_next_step: Two concrete avenues were identified but not exhausted. First, the SECO 'nationaler Lohnrechner' (national salary calculator), which is referenced by SECO as distinct from the FSO's gross-only Salarium, and which is expected to produce a cantonal net figure from published rates. Second, cantonal tax-office calculators (for example Zurich, Basel-Stadt or Vaud), which are official government tools publishing a net-for-gross calculation with stated canton, tax year, marital status and church-tax assumptions. A canton-specific route is the correct one for Switzerland, because cantonal and municipal rates differ enough that no national net figure would be useful for a break-even calculation anyway.

field_mapping.net_monthly_income: career.net_monthly_income (topic: net_monthly_income) - NO usable national figure; see the two bracketing thresholds in 020_net_monthly_income.json and the gross figures in 010_gross_monthly_income.json

notes: This artifact records an honest negative result with a specific, technical diagnosis: Swiss net wage data is COLLECTED by the federal statistical office but is not PUBLISHED in the accessible outputs, and the most tempting source for it (the FSO's 'Lohnrechner', Salarium) is gross-only despite its name. Any Swiss net salary figure circulating online - and there are many - comes from private calculators, not from the Swiss authorities, and should not be treated as official. Switzerland is the weakest of the four countries in this corpus for official net evidence. Note for context: this is a design consequence, not an oversight - income tax in Switzerland is levied by cantons and municipalities, so a single national net figure would be actively misleading for a cost-vs-salary comparison, and this is a much stronger reason for the corpus to treat Switzerland as cantonal-only than the absence of a published number is.
evidence_limitations: Negative finding. The diagnosis of 'no net table in the FSO published outputs' is established from reading the FSO pages and from querying the PX-Web data cube index directly, but it is not a proof that no net figure exists anywhere in Swiss official publishing - for example in a cantonal statistical office's own analysis, which is exactly how the one net data point in 020_net_monthly_income.json was obtained. No figure was invented to fill this gap, and no median was interpolated from the two published distribution thresholds.
